payload.text:
I reviewed search-filters against main (2 commits). The tests pass, but **I'd hold the merge. There's a SQL injection in the new free-text search.** I didn't change anything.

**Blocker: `src/query.js`, the term clause**
```js
clauses.push("name ILIKE '%" + term + "%'");
```
This pastes the search term straight into the SQL. The README says never to do that. A term like `' OR 1=1 --` breaks out of the string. It should use a placeholder like the category filter does:
```js
params.push('%' + term + '%');
clauses.push(`name ILIKE $${params.length}`);
```
If you want `%` and `_` in a search to match literally, escape them in the term and add `ESCAPE '\'`. Also, a term that's only spaces currently trims to `''` and becomes `ILIKE '%%'`, which matches everything. It's worth skipping the clause when the trimmed term is empty.

The tests didn't catch this because they only check that the SQL text matches `/name ILIKE/`. Please add a check that the term ends up in `params` and that the SQL has `$n` instead of the term itself. An injection-style term would make a good test case.

**Should fix**
- **Renamed export:** `buildFilters` is now `buildWhere`. Nothing in this repo still calls the old name, but anything outside it that imports `buildFilters` will break. That's a breaking change, so either keep the old name as an alias or note it in the changelog.
- **Deleted test:** the in-stock test was removed rather than renamed. The "combine with AND" test only covers it partly. I'd add it back.
- **`relevance` sort uses `rank DESC`:** that's also the default sort. Nothing in this branch adds a `rank` column, so unless the query you're putting this into already has one, every default search will fail. Please confirm.

**Minor**
- In `paginate.js`, `MAX_PAGE` actually limits page size, so `MAX_PAGE_SIZE` would be a clearer name. Using `| 0` turns `'abc'` and `NaN` into 1, which is fine, but numbers above about 2.1 billion overflow. Also, page numbers have no upper limit, so a huge page gives a huge offset. That may be worth capping.
- The sort list in `sort.js` looks good: unknown values fall back to relevance, so nothing from the request gets into the SQL. There are no tests for it yet.
- The changelog mentions "sort orders" but not pagination or the rename.

Fix the injection and its test before you merge; the other items are small.
